headline: Earnings grow as Textron begins sale of Industrial unit
summary_short: Revenue rose 3.0% y/y to $3,827M and diluted EPS grew 5.2% to $1.42, while adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS rose to $1.62 from $1.55 a year ago. Textron reiterated full-year 2026 guidance and initiated a sale process for its Industrial segment.
summary_long: Revenue grew 3.0% y/y to $3,827M as Bell (+6%), Textron Systems (+7%), and Aviation (+1%) revenue gains offset roughly flat consolidated segment profit ($353M): Aviation and Bell profit fell on manufacturing inefficiencies and unfavorable program mix, while Systems and Industrial profit rose on lower R&D and higher pricing. Diluted EPS rose 5.2% to $1.42; adjusted EPS rose to $1.62 from $1.55. Manufacturing operating cash flow fell to $235M from $395M on working-capital timing, even as the company repurchased $209M of stock. Cash was $1,606M and equity $8,054M, both up y/y. Textron reiterated FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance of $5.39-$5.59 ($6.40-$6.60 adjusted) and cash-flow guidance of $700-$800M, and initiated a sale process for the Industrial segment.

drivers.explanation: CEO Lisa Atherton cited revenue growth across all manufacturing segments, progress on Bell's MV-75 Cheyenne (production of key long-lead parts), and Aviation's Ascend program delivering its first five aircraft to NetJets.
Textron initiated a sale process for its Industrial segment (Kautex and Textron Specialized Vehicles); no financial terms, buyer, or timeline were disclosed in this release.

Growth was led by Bell (+6% y/y, higher military H-1 and MV-75 volume) and Textron Systems (+7%, higher armored-vehicle and ATAC volume); Aviation grew a smaller 1% on higher pricing partly offset by lower Citation and defense-jet volume.

Consolidated segment profit was roughly flat y/y ($353M vs $352M): Aviation and Bell profit fell on manufacturing inefficiencies and unfavorable program/mix, while Industrial and Systems profit rose on higher pricing (including recovered tariffs) and lower R&D spending.
Not explained in the release; Textron does not discuss EBITDA as such.
Not explained in the release; Textron does not report a standalone gross-profit line, and cost commentary was limited to segment-level pricing/mix and R&D discussion.

Net income growth (+1.2% y/y) tracks pretax income growth (+1.0% y/y, to $304M) with a roughly stable effective tax rate (~18.4% vs ~18.6% a year earlier); the release gives no separate tax narrative.

Not explained in the release as a single cause; quarterly operating cash flow was actually lower y/y ($235M manufacturing vs $395M), so the y/y cash gain reflects the trailing period's broader activity, not this quarter's flow.
